explainer27.headline: 27% is the Foundations number. CCAR-P has no 27% domain.
paragraphs: 'Agentic Architecture & Orchestration: 27%' is a real, official figure. It belongs to the Foundations exam (CCAR-F), not to Professional. Anthropic published it in the CCAR-F launch guide on 12 March 2026 ('27% of scored content') and kept it in CCAR-F v1.0 (July 2026): 27/18/20/20/15 across 5 domains, 60 items, and 4 scenarios drawn from a bank of 6.

CCAR-P did not exist until about 8 July 2026. For roughly four months, 27% was the only official Claude Architect blueprint, so every guide, repo and practice trainer written between March and July used it, legitimately, for Foundations. The most direct source of the phrase 'Agentic Architecture 27%' is probably a Foundations trainer you already have. A practice file titled 'Claude Certified Architect · Foundations — Practice Exam' tags every D1 item 'Agentic Architecture' and says its mix 'matches the published weights exactly (27/18/20/20/15)', and the official CCAR-F naming uses the same words. Many community repos also keep the Foundations blueprint one click from their Professional pages, and the legacy 'CCA-F' label makes the two exams look like one family with one blueprint. If your practice exam is titled 'Foundations', uses Task 1.x labels, or says 'weights match 27/18/20/20/15', it is a CCAR-F trainer.

The CCAR-P v1.0 guide has 7 domains weighted 17/13/19/16/14/14/7, and none of them is called Agentic Architecture. Agentic and multi-agent design appear as 2 of the 6 objectives inside D1 Solution Design & Architecture (17%). The heaviest domain is D3 Integration at 19%. Evaluation, Governance and Stakeholder work (D4–D6) together make up 44% of CCAR-P, and Foundations material barely covers them.

There is also an extraction trap. If you run the official CCAR-P PDF through pdftotext -layout, the weight column in the blueprint table shifts down one row: 17% prints on the header line and D1 appears as '13%'. The per-domain headings settle it ('Domain 1: Solution Design & Architecture (17%)'). If you saw some other number, 17% (D1) or 19% (Integration) is the likely candidate, but that is a guess, not a confirmed source.

Numbering is a separate tell. CCAR-F numbers its task statements officially (for example 'Task Statement 2.1'). The CCAR-P guide lists its 38 objectives as unnumbered bullets, and the IDs 1.1–7.3 used in this portal are a study convention. A source that quotes 'official' CCAR-P task numbers, or builds mocks on named scenarios, is carrying Foundations structure over. Use Foundations material for vocabulary and timing only, never to calibrate your readiness.

spot_checklist: The blueprint reads 27/18/20/20/15, or lists five domains with 'Agentic Architecture & Orchestration' first.
Mocks are organised around named scenarios (Customer Support Resolution Agent, Code Generation with Claude Code, Multi-Agent Research System, and so on), or it says '4 of 6' or '4 of 8' scenarios.
Format facts say 60 items, $125 or $99, or 'one correct answer out of four'.
It cites 'Task Statement 1.x' numbering or the CCA-F/CCAR-F code, and spends most of its time on tool_choice, stop_reason loops, CLAUDE.md hierarchy and CLI flags.
It has little or nothing on evaluation thresholds, governance controls, compliance mapping, stakeholder communication or RAG design, which make up about half of CCAR-P.

items: Confirm the booking, your time zone and the reschedule deadline (use 48 hours).
Check that your registration name exactly matches your government ID.
Confirm your partner discount was applied, and keep the receipt.
Choose OnVUE or a test centre. For OnVUE, run the Pearson system test on the exact machine and network.
Form A is on the calendar at about 55% of your timeline, and no later than T-7.
The Form C dress-rehearsal window opens (T-7 to T-3). Sit it under exam conditions.
Write your final remediation list of no more than 5 objectives, and do nothing else new.
Plan the room: one monitor, no second screen, a clear desk, no papers or phone within reach, and a closed door.
Arrange to be undisturbed for about 135 minutes of seat time.
Decide after Form C (by T-3): if readiness is still Not yet, reschedule before the 48-hour deadline.
Start the taper: no new material and no sealed form after T-2.
Daily: cheat-sheet night-before mode, cue flashcards, and clear the spaced-review queue.
One 10-item pacing drill at 1:45 per item.
Re-read the trap codes you fall for most and their counter-rules.
Light review only: the laws, trigger words and your top 3 traps. Stop by early evening.
Re-run the OnVUE system test. Turn off OS updates, close background apps and silence notifications.
Charge the laptop and use wired power. Prefer a wired network connection.
Put your ID next to the machine. Sleep.
Start check-in early; setup and room scans take time. Allow about 135 minutes in total.
Once seated, commit to the plan: about 1:45 per item on the first pass, checkpoints at 17/30:00, 34/60:00, 51/90:00 and 63/110:00.
On every item: count first on multi-response, find the binding constraint, then eliminate options by naming each trap.
Past 3 minutes: best answer, flag, move on. Leave nothing blank.
Last 10 minutes: flagged items, then recheck the selection count on every multi-response item. Change an answer only for a specific error you have found.
Record your pass/fail result, scaled score and percent-correct by domain. The domain percentages are diagnostic only.
If you passed: claim the Credly badge and set a renewal reminder for month 10 (validity is 12 months, renewal free if on time).
If you did not pass: the first retake wait is 14 days (then 30, then 90), with at most 4 attempts per rolling 12 months. Rebuild the plan from the domain percentages, weighted by the domain weights.
Appeals must be filed within 14 days.
You accepted an NDA, so do not share or reconstruct live items.

pacing.perItem: About 1:45 per item on the first pass (110 minutes ÷ 63), which keeps 10 minutes in reserve; the raw average is 1:54 (120 ÷ 63)
checkpoints: First pass complete through item 63 by 110:00 elapsed (10:00 left for flags and counts)
rules: On multi-response items, read the 'select N' count before the stem, and check it again before you move on.
Read the question line, then find the binding constraint, then eliminate options by naming each one's trap, then choose.
Past 3 minutes, enter your best answer, flag the item and move on. Never flag an item with no answer.
If you are more than 5 minutes behind at a checkpoint, eliminate two options, pick, flag and move on until you are back on pace.
Answer every item. The CCAR-F guide scores blanks as incorrect with no guessing penalty, and no penalty is documented for CCAR-P.
Use the reserved time for flagged items first, then a pass over every multi-response count.
Change an answer only when you find a specific error, such as a missed constraint word, a wrong count or an assumption the stem never stated.
Anthropic does not publish item weights, so treat every item as equal and do not sink time into one hard stem.
Do not convert 720 into an allowed number of misses mid-exam. It is a scaled score, not 72%.
